races.name: MJG Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Rossa Ryan who needs cover and a strong pace to reel in; sim-going figures (1W1P from 8) are modest but relevant, and 21 days since last run is straightforward; handicap mark of 67 is workable if the front end burns.

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Clive Cox in fair recent form (2/20 past 14 days) and this three-year-old won over this exact six-furlong trip on good ground last time; soft-going form is thin (0W0P on similar), but draw five is workable and Hector Crouch gives him a sharp pilot.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (t) and returned to winning ways over six furlongs on soft ground two runs ago, making conditions here genuinely relevant; Mark Rimell has had a quiet 14-day spell (0/6) and the eight-day turnaround is quick, though Callum Rodriguez is a capable partner.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old who has won three of her last six including back-to-back six-furlong victories on good and soft; Lewis Edmunds partners a horse drawn ten on a flat, straight track which poses no concern, and Rod Millman's 2/24 fortnight suggests the yard is ticking over.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who drops back to six furlongs from a recent run at the trip; her two placed efforts on soft/good-to-soft over five furlongs are a positive going note, though William Carver's trainer (0/4 in 14 days) is quiet and she is yet to win in six starts.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers (b) and has won twice recently at six furlongs on good ground, giving her a live profile on form; the step into softer conditions is unproven (1/9 on similar) and she is held up from a draw of nine, needing a strong pace to deliver her running.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison keeps this filly busy (LR:14d, 2/15 in 14 days) and she placed over five furlongs on good ground last season, but she is a natural hold-up horse who cannot get to the rear of this field because too many confirmed hold-up types are present — she is likely to race in a middle position that is not her optimum, which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is in solid form (3/34 in 14 days) and Charles Bishop is a capable front-running pilot; however, Eightthreeone's recent form string (326544) shows she has not converted her pace into wins, and contested leadership against Maid In Devon on soft ground is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Sixty-day absence is the key question for this hold-up type who placed at seven furlongs on soft ground two runs ago, showing he handles cut; Callum Shepherd's mount needs a strong pace to deliver late and the layoff introduces freshness risk at the foot of the weights.

runners_data.name: Mollstar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's yard is the meeting's busiest (6/42 in 14 days) which is a positive yard-form angle; Mollstar races prominently, ran second over six furlongs on good last time and draws four which is workable, though a soft-going win has not yet materialised (0W0P on similar).

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: David Evans has 2/23 in 14 days and Pat Cosgrave is a seasoned handler of prominent racers; Guernsey Angel placed over six furlongs on good-to-soft two runs ago but has otherwise been well beaten in this company, and a wide draw of 12 means she will need to find her spot quickly.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 2/47 in 14 days is modest but the trainer regularly runs horses here; Pilgrim's Progress has three placed efforts in her last five but has not won in eight starts — a front-prominent runner who needs things to fall right and whose soft-ground record (0W0P) offers little reassurance.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR=70 and has won twice and placed three times on soft or good-to-soft in fifteen runs, giving him the standout conditions profile; Rachel Cook & John Bridger's 2/8 fortnight is solid, and Jack Callan from the wide draw 13 will likely sit just off the front two in a tactical position that suits.

races.paceDynamic: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over Salisbury's straight six furlongs on Good To Soft ground, guaranteeing a genuine, honest gallop rather than a dawdle. Madman and Bold Shout will push forward from prominent positions and add further pressure into the early stages, meaning the pace is unlikely to let up and any leader will need to be durable under handicap conditions. This field carries more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their natural positions — Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are most likely to actually secure the lead, with Madman and Bold Shout forced slightly wider or behind early. A genuinely contested pace on soft-ish ground over six furlongs historically plays into the hands of hold-up or late-finishing horses who can be delivered with a single sustained run, though Maid In Devon's proven class in this role — and her win record on similar ground — makes her the principal threat to that generality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Maid In Devon breaks cleanly and controls the pace without being harried into unsustainably fast fractions.
scenarios.body: Maid In Devon dictates from her wide draw, setting a true but measured gallop and kicking off the bend; her soft-ground win record (1W1P on similar) shows she handles these conditions and her recent hat-trick of wins confirms she is in the form of her life.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the front two tie each other up and Madman or Bold Shout travel powerfully just off the pace before producing a decisive challenge.
scenarios.body: Madman's OR=70 and four soft/good-to-soft placings from fifteen runs give him the quality and proven conditions profile to pick up the pieces; Bold Shout's recent six-furlong win on good ground and Clive Cox's sharp trainer stats make him the clear second string in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the dual front-runner battle burns genuinely hot and the field strings out, leaving a gap for patient hold-up horses to run through.
scenarios.body: Red Snapper and Pull The Rug both race from the rear and have course-distance-similar going form; if the pace is truly injurious to the leaders, a single well-timed challenge from off the pace can land the spoils.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Eightthreeone fails to fire and Maid In Devon is left in front at a slow early tempo, compressing the field and turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a bunched late dash on soft ground, heavier-weighted, higher-rated runners like Madman and Bold Shout hold an advantage in a rough-and-tumble finish, while Nebbia — though racing out of her natural hold-up role — could find herself ideally positioned if the pace is pedestrian.

watchPoints.text: Maid In Devon vs Eightthreeone — watch which of these two front-runners gets their nose in front inside the first furlong, as the one who concedes the rail will burn energy challenging and may not see out the six furlongs on soft ground.

Madman (draw 13) — if Jack Callan angles across quickly to track the leaders from the outside draw, he could slot into a perfect stalking position; if he is caught wide throughout, his chance is compromised despite his superior soft-ground record.

Nebbia — watch where Harry Davies actually settles her in running; she is a hold-up type who cannot get her natural position in this pace-heavy field, so her actual race position will be a key indicator of whether she has any realistic chance in the straight.

Red Snapper — blinkers applied and two recent wins on good, but her soft-going profile (1/9) is untested at this level; if the ground is riding closer to soft than good-to-soft after earlier races, monitor whether she is travelling comfortably in the latter stages.

White Ladder — 60-day absence from John Ryan's yard (2/8 in 14 days) means freshness is a genuine wild card; if he shows early exuberance and Callum Shepherd cannot settle him in a hold-up position, his stamina for a strong-paced six furlongs on soft ground becomes a concern.

races.name: PKF Francis Clark Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Bounced back well for Sheena West with back-to-back wins on Good, but similar-going record is a stark 1W0P from 10 starts on Soft-equivalent — the step up in ground moisture is a real question, and his prominent style puts him right in the early traffic scrum.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Pep
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends him back after 13 days with Rossa Ryan booked — a clear upgrade — and recent form shows consistent placing (2-3-2-3) with a soft-ground third on the board; travels prominently and should handle the pace battle better than some rivals, making him the Strand's primary danger flag.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave engaged for David Evans (2/23 in 14 days) on a horse who won on Good over 6f and has two Soft efforts — a sixth and a fifth — suggesting the ground is manageable but not optimal; drops back from midfield position to work from just off the pace and the Strand's top pick despite low confidence given inconsistent recent form (2-2-7-1-5-6).

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's four-year-old arrives with a headgear change (p — first-time hood?) and a mixed recent profile, but that 1/7f/SOF win proves he can handle this ground; holds-up and needs the race to develop in front of him — if prominent runners burn each other, his late rattle is credible.

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: 35-day break is the headline here — longest layoff in the field — and Brian Toomey's 0/3 in 14 days offers no short-term confidence; hood retained, style is hold-up, and he needs a pace collapse to be involved at Salisbury over 6f.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's eight-year-old runs again quickly (13 days) wearing blinkers, and prominent style means he'll be in the early battle for position from stall 3; soft-ground record (0W0P from 4 tries) is a concern on a card where conditions are consistently testing, and he may weaken through the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner from the perfect stall 5 draws, wearing a tongue-tie and given 24 days to recover; similar-going record is minimal (0W0P from 1 start) and dropping from 7f to 6f is a positive, but he sets the pace everyone else will target — his stamina on Soft ground at 6f is unproven.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old arrives on the back of back-to-back wins at 6f on Good, carrying top weight at 130lbs but rated the lowest in the race (OR=76); similar-going record on Soft is thin, and from stall 9 he'll need to work to find a prominent pitch — if he does, recent form makes him dangerous, but the ground is an open query.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Michael Blake's eight-year-old has strong form on Good — winning twice and placing — but the two Soft starts produced an eighth and a fourth, suggesting he wants the ground quicker; holds up from stall 1 (the inside but no material advantage on this flat track) and must hope for a pace collapse that his going profile suggests he may not fully capitalise on.

races.paceDynamic: Padua is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawing from stall 5 on this flat Salisbury 6f, should secure an uncontested lead at a tempo that he controls rather than one forced upon him. Behind him, a prominent cluster of Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, and Safari Dream will jostle for the best early berths, creating genuine congestion 2-3 furlongs out as four horses chase three realistic prominent positions — expect shuffling and interference through that phase. Supreme King (midfield) and the hold-up trio of Rare Change, The Quiet Gent, and Under The Twilight will be angling for late runs into whatever gaps survive that scrimmage. The soft-ish going (officially Good to Soft throughout the card) will blunt finishing kicks and favour horses travelling prominently rather than closing from off the pace, meaning the prominent-to-midfield profile — horses who can sit just off Padua without burning fuel in the early scramble — is the most dangerous tactical position in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Padua Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Padua sets a measured, uncontested pace and the prominent challengers settle sweetly just off him.
scenarios.body: Padua's lone lead at a Soft-ground tempo produces a truly-run but not fast 6f, leaving plenty for horses travelling prominently in second-to-fourth to find late; the early-berth scramble among Sergeant Pep, Tenbob Tommy, and Baldomero resolves by halfway and the most economically-ridden of that group runs through the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble burns Padua and the front-runners out, leaving a genuine late window.
scenarios.body: Congestion and competition for the lead drains the prominent ranks by the 2f pole, creating a rare late run on a course that usually punishes closers; Under The Twilight and Rare Change, who have the form and fitness to finish powerfully, would be the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Safari Dream Front-Runs Rivals Into Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Safari Dream's back-to-back winning form emboldens connections to press Padua aggressively from stall 9.
scenarios.body: Safari Dream's recent course-and-distance form at Good gives him natural speed, and if he forces a faster pace alongside Padua, the race becomes a genuine test of stamina on Soft ground that suits the horse arriving fresh from midfield; Supreme King, who has won on Soft over 6f, would be the primary threat from just behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicapper's Field, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If pace is moderate throughout and all running styles converge in a tight finish with little to separate them.
scenarios.body: A soft-ground handicap at this level can compress the field when no horse truly dominates — draw, positioning luck, and jockey decisions (Rossa Ryan, Pat Cosgrave the standout bookings) become the deciding margin; the horse who gets the clearest run through traffic 2f out wins a photo.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic 2-3 furlongs out: with Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, and Safari Dream all wanting early position behind Padua, watch for crowding and interference through the midrace phase — horses caught wide or checked here lose the race.

Sergeant Pep's market move: Rossa Ryan's booking for Clive Cox is the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — if the market shortens him significantly before post time, treat it as a live signal that connections believe the ground and conditions suit.

Safari Dream's price vs. recent form: two wins on the bounce may attract punter attention, but both came on Good ground — if conditions remain Good to Soft (as the going report consistently shows), assess whether his market price reflects the genuine ground uncertainty.

Supreme King's soft-ground form: the Strand's top pick has run six times on Soft-equivalent and managed only 1W1P from 15 starts — the confidence rating is already flagged low, and backers should be aware that today's conditions represent a genuine statistical weakness.

Padua's pace control is the structural key: if he is allowed to stride on unchallenged through the first 2f, every other scenario weakens — watch his early splits to judge whether the race is truly run at a sustainable or artificially slow tempo.

races.name: Happy 40th Birthday Kevin Baker Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Persian Land
runners_data.note: Lightly campaigned 2yo trained by David Evans who snapped a sequence with a win over 6f on Soft 15 days ago; midfield style is well-suited to the pace scenario here, and stepping up to 7f on Good to Soft is an uncomplicated ask given his dam's stamina influence; Callum Rodriguez takes the ride for a yard firing 2/23 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Absolute Diamond
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip (7f Soft) last time out for David Evans, giving the trainer a dual-pronged attack with Persian Land; midfield style means she tracks the pace battle without being drawn into it, and her two placings on soft-adjacent ground underpin confidence; Pat Cosgrave is a significant booking at this level.

runners_data.name: Hello You Ten
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who must lead from stall 2 but carries an explicit fade flag — over 6f on Good ground she faded, and the step to 7f on a more testing surface only exacerbates that concern; William Carver is a claim rider for a trainer hitting 2/14 over the fortnight, which provides mild support, but the profile screams "pacemaker."

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Races in a hood and has been beaten since May across five runs, including two over this trip at Sandown on Standard going; the fade flag is prominent, and contesting the lead with Hello You Ten on Good to Soft ground over 7f is likely to suit neither horse; Jack Callan partners for a trainer running at 2/29 over 14 days — faint support but structural concerns dominate.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Run just four days ago — the quick turnaround is a concern for a 2yo in soft ground — and his five-run record shows zero placed finishes on soft-adjacent conditions; hold-up style is genuine but the form string (79904) does not suggest he can capitalise even if the pace scenario broke his way; Lewis Edmunds rides.

runners_data.name: Oxber Flyer
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no OR, no form string, lightly raced flag, and going marked UNKNOWN, which means there is no basis for confidence; trainer Charlie Clover has limited recent runners (2/4 over 14 days) and Callum Shepherd takes a speculative ride; cannot be assessed meaningfully and must be treated as an outsider with upside risk only.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with six runs, all at sprint trips (5f-6f), stepping up to 7f for the first time with a fade flag attached — the extra furlong on Good to Soft ground is a significant unknown; Isobelle Chalmers claims 7lb but the horse has placed nowhere in eight attempts on soft-adjacent ground; likely to find position and then struggle to sustain it.

runners_data.name: Lushill
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's named danger, and the profile is credible: placed at 7f and 6f on Good and Standard, with a recent second over 7f on Good ground, she handles the trip and goes forward naturally; William Cox rides for the Moore yard that also runs Our Fella, but Lushill's form figures over distance are superior; the widest draw (10) is neutral on Salisbury's straight course.

runners_data.name: The Kalonji Man
runners_data.note: Form string (04869) is poor and his natural style is midfield; he has been redistributed to a hold-up map position because the field is light on genuine hold-up types, but he is not a natural rear-ranger and should not be expected to produce a closing run from the back — discount this positional label; blinkers are applied and trainer Hannon sends runners regularly (2/47 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Grapple
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run — a 12th over 7f on Good ground — and carries a fade flag and hood (first-time blinkers); Ralph Beckett's yard is in strong form (9/45 over 14 days) which is the main positive, but 56 days off, a single poor run and a first-time headgear combination make this a major unknown; Hector Crouch takes the ride.

races.paceDynamic: Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from stalls 5 and 2 respectively, creating a genuinely contested pace on Salisbury's straight 7f in Good to Soft ground. That battle for supremacy is likely to produce an honest, sustained gallop rather than a falsely slow tempo, with neither rider having any tactical reason to concede the rail. Our Fella will push forward from stall 6 to sit prominently just off the two leaders, and Lushill will look to hold a handy position from the outside, meaning the prominent berths will be well-populated and competitive throughout. The race shape that emerges — contested pace, honest gallop on soft-ish ground over 7f — squarely favours horses who can travel in midfield, conserve energy through the early exchanges, and pick up when the front-runners come back to the field in the final two furlongs; the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all sustain their positions, and among those likely to actually secure a forward pitch, Our Fella (prominent, drawn 6) and Lushill (drawn 10, progressive) look best placed, while the pace-pressers Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten carry clear fade flags. Persian Land (midfield) and Absolute Diamond (midfield) are positioned to exploit any collapse in the leaders, with the race shape favouring the stalking mid-division profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfielders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten burn each other off and the honest gallop on Good to Soft ground drains the prominent runners in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fade predictably given both carry fade flags, leaving Persian Land and Absolute Diamond to pick them off in the closing stages from their energy-conserving midfield positions; soft ground extends the advantage of those who have been patient, and Salisbury's rising finish further punishes horses who have emptied.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is less intense than expected — one of the front-runners is outpaced early or settles — allowing a prominent type to get a soft lead or box seat and control their own energy expenditure.
scenarios.body: Lushill, who has placed at 7f-8f in similar ground and holds a clean record at the trip, would benefit most from a scenario where prominent runners are not all fighting for the same space; her consistency over 7f and positive recent form make her the pick of the prominent brigade if the pace softens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of Minzaal Time or Hello You Ten breaks sharply and dominates unchallenged while the other fails to press, creating a falsely slow early tempo.
scenarios.body: In this low-probability shape the winner would need to be a front-runner who can dictate and sustain — Hello You Ten's trainer form is better placed this fortnight but both carry fade flags that make lasting home over 7f in soft ground unlikely; the scenario requires conditions to play into their hands and the pace battle to fizzle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Flourish From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field into a sprint home and a hold-up horse finds clear daylight late.
scenarios.body: The Kalonji Man is redistributed and not a natural hold-up type, making this scenario structurally unlikely to produce its supposed beneficiary; Courage Best has zero placed runs from five attempts on soft-adjacent ground and is dropping to a low-traffic position, so the late-closer shape lacks credible horses to deliver it.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hello You Ten or Minzaal Time secures the early lead unchallenged — if one breaks sharply and the other fails to press, the pace scenario shifts and a prominent racer could benefit with much less pace pressure than modelled.

Grapple (first-time blinkers, 56-day absence, Beckett yard in form) is a form unknown who could outrun odds if the headgear produces an improved performance — monitor the betting market for any significant movement on this runner before post time.

Our Fella stretches to 7f for the first time from stall 6; if she jumps quickly and fills a handy spot without fighting for the lead, she could outperform her fade flag — but if she is pressed early, her form over the extra furlong is untested and the flag becomes real.

Oxber Flyer (no OR, no form, going UNKNOWN) is a complete wildcard from a small yard — any unexpected market support should be treated as a possible stable confidence signal worth noting, even if the form book offers no foundation.

Persian Land and Absolute Diamond represent a dual Evans yard attack; if both are in the market, consider whether the trainer has a preferred runner — Rodriguez on Persian Land (the higher-rated, more recent winner) suggests the stable's primary focus.

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old prominent racer whose best form has come around 21-22f; Josephine Gordon keeps this simple by stalking the pace, but sim-going figures of 2/6 with no wins or placings in similar conditions are a concern, and 20 days' freshness may not compensate for the class deficit against Amiloc.

runners_data.name: Quickthorn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old front-runner for Hughie Morrison with a single soft-ground run in his recent history (5th over 16f); he will press Amiloc hard from the front but OR 108 and a recent form string of 5461/5 suggest he is more likely to shape the race than win it.

runners_data.name: Lion's Pride
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for the Gosden yard stepping up significantly in trip from his last three runs over 12f — all on Good ground — and 133 days off the track is a significant unknown; Robert Havlin's patient approach is the right tactics for this pace scenario, and if the step to 1m6f on soft suits his stamina profile he is the most dangerous closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 114 and a natural front-runner who will contest the lead with Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer; his sim-going record of 2/5 includes a place finish, and Ralph Beckett's strong 14-day strike rate (9/45) adds confidence, though form figures of 4-66U7 raise questions about whether his best days are behind him at four.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: The least exposed of the front-runners on OR 93 but recent form of 4-4070 and a tendency to finish mid-to-rear over shorter trips gives little encouragement; the blinker headgear may sharpen early enthusiasm but risks ensuring he burns out quickly, making him a pacemaker for others rather than a genuine contender over this stamina-testing trip.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer — line up over 1m6f on Good To Soft ground at Salisbury, making a strong, contested gallop a near-certainty from the outset. Amiloc (OR 114, Ralph Beckett) and Quickthorn (OR 108) are the classier pace-setters and will both want to dictate, meaning neither can simply bowl along unchallenged; Nightime Dancer (OR 93) adds a third body pressing forward, further ensuring the pace will be genuine and sustained. Soul Icon tracks prominently and will be carried along by the tempo, while Lion's Pride is the lone hold-up horse and is the one runner whose energy reserves will be intact when the pressure bites in the final quarter-mile. This race shape strongly favours a deep-staying, hold-up or late-running profile — the front three are burning energy fighting each other, and the horse who can arrive fresh and powerful into the straight, rather than having already scrapped for position, carries the biggest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Tie Each Other
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc, Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer push hard early and collectively set a pace that stretches stamina to breaking point.
scenarios.body: The three leaders trade blows across the first mile of a stamina test in soft ground, with each spending vital energy contesting position rather than conserving it; by the home straight two or more of the pace-setters are treading water. Lion's Pride, held up off the pace by Havlin, arrives with a clean run and picks up the weakening leaders in the final furlong, while Soul Icon — who has tracked the pace — may also stay on if the leaders fade early enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc asserts dominance early and the other front-runners are unable or unwilling to match his stride, allowing him to control a measured gallop.
scenarios.body: Amiloc, the highest-rated runner at OR 114 with Rossa Ryan in the plate and Ralph Beckett's strong recent strike rate, sets a controlled tempo that plays to his stamina rather than burning it; with no genuine pace duel developing, the speed advantage he built in the early stages never fully dissipates. In this shape a front-runner who dictates on his own terms and gets a breather mid-race is dangerous, and Lion's Pride's hold-up profile may find less ground to make up but arrives too late if the tempo was never truly brutal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind Favour Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so savage that even the prominent trackers — including Soul Icon — are compromised, leaving only the deepest stayer standing.
scenarios.body: Nightime Dancer, with a blinker headgear flag and a low OR of 93, may force an unsustainably frenetic opening, dragging Amiloc and Quickthorn into a war of attrition over the first mile in soft ground; any horse that tracked the leaders closely is then vulnerable in the closing stages. In this scenario Lion's Pride, given a masterclass patient ride by Robert Havlin for the powerful Gosden stable, sweeps through beaten horses and lands the spoils, with the race effectively over for all the pace-involved horses by the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Idle
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners collectively slow the tempo — jockeys unwilling to go hard — and the race becomes a tactical crawl before a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over 1m6f on soft ground would compress the field and turn it into a test of pure speed in the final two furlongs; this benefits horses with a higher cruising speed and the class to quicken, rather than genuine stayers grinding it out. Amiloc's OR 114 gives him the best finishing speed in the field under this shape, though this scenario runs against all available pace evidence given three confirmed front-runners who naturally want to go forward.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Amiloc or Quickthorn blinks first in the battle for the lead — whichever one is forced to race wide or fight hardest for position in the first half-mile will be the one most vulnerable late on.

Lion's Pride is 133 days off the course and stepping up from 12f to 1m6f; if the layoff has left him ring-rusty or the trip proves beyond him, the hold-up scenario collapses and Amiloc's rivals thin dramatically.

Nightime Dancer's blinkers flag the possibility of a reckless early pace — if he bolts into the lead and drags the others into an unsustainable gallop in the first half-mile, soft ground will ruthlessly expose every front-runner's stamina ceiling.

Soul Icon has registered zero wins and zero places in six comparable soft-ground runs; if conditions continue to ease toward Soft proper (the going report shows Good To Soft across the card), her chance of upsetting the market leaders diminishes further.

runners_data.name: Mid Flight
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up profile for Havlin and the Charalambous & Clutterbuck yard, but all three turf runs have come over shorter distances than today's 1m2f, and soft-ground form is limited to one effort (finishing fifth at Sandown); needs the pace to collapse in front of her.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on soft for Balding and Carver is a compelling credential here, but a noted tendency to fade in the finish is a serious concern when the pace promises to be fierce throughout; has to overcome the pattern of emptying late to justify his danger tag.

runners_data.name: Fanciulla Del West
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's mare has placed twice over 1m4f on good and shapes as a genuine stayer by profile, but her five-runner recent form string shows inconsistency in finishing position; front-running style means she must absorb early challenges from at least three rivals, and her turf soft-ground experience is minimal.

runners_data.name: Miss Guinevere
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' filly has shown ability to settle in midfield and finish off her races, and a third on good ground over 10f is her best effort; headgear flag suggests she needs mental management, and trainer's recent 14-day strike rate (1/15) is modest.

runners_data.name: Gatlinburg
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 105 days for Attwater, and genuinely a hold-up horse by nature — placed in the midfield section of the map because the field is packed with even further hold-up types, but her actual role will be rearmost; soft-ground form (two from five relevant runs) is moderate at best, and the layoff adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Letter
runners_data.note: Menuisier's filly has placed twice over 10f on good ground and handles soft, making her one of the more interesting hold-up profiles in the race; 55 days off could mean she arrives fresh, and the trainer's quiet recent spell (0/24 in 14 days) is a minor negative flag.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection, and form of 222128 shows admirable consistency — the sole win came over 9f on good, and soft-ground exposure is limited across ten relevant runs (1W 2P from 10); Portman and Davies combine well, and a low draw of 3 should allow him to establish position cleanly.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's runner brings form figures that trend downward (3-8654) and his four most recent runs are all on good ground at 8f — stepping up in trip on softer terrain is a double unknown, and Edmunds will need to manage him carefully in a pace battle he may not be able to sustain.

runners_data.name: Eljowhary
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 70 for Eve Johnson Houghton, but form figures of 66400 tell a story of steady decline, and two of those runs have come over today's 1m2f trip on Flat/Stalls ground; flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a critical concern when four rivals intend to press from the front.

runners_data.name: Sax Avoidance
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile from Charlie Pike's yard with only three runs to his name, all at 10f and all on good or artificial surfaces — today's softer going is untested and represents the key question mark; form of 543 shows gradual improvement but nothing to suggest he can beat more experienced rivals on this surface.

races.paceDynamic: Four confirmed front-runners — Fanciulla Del West, Relentless Hero, Takeitorleaveit, and Next Guilian — will battle for position from the outset at Salisbury over 1m2f on good-to-soft ground, guaranteeing a strong, searching gallop that will expose any stamina limitations. The field contains more front-running types than the track can comfortably accommodate at the head of affairs; Takeitorleaveit and Fanciulla Del West are likeliest to actually secure prominent positions given their recent consistency, while Relentless Hero and Next Guilian face a genuine battle to get their natural slots and may be forced wider or harder than ideal. Eljowhary, racing prominently with a noted tendency to fade, adds further pressure to the early exchanges but is unlikely to sustain it into the final quarter-mile on this ground. With stamina at a premium and the pace almost certain to be unrelenting, this race shape heavily favours genuine stayers and hold-up horses who can be delivered fresh into the straight — those racing off the pace and finishing through beaten rivals rather than those expending energy fighting for position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Stamps Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners push each other along at a true gallop and the race is run to suit genuine staying profiles.
scenarios.body: The early scrapping between Fanciulla Del West, Relentless Hero, Takeitorleaveit, and Next Guilian ensures the pace never relents, leaving the leaders vulnerable inside the final furlong on soft-ish ground; horses delivered late and fresh gain a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit or Fanciulla Del West establishes clean control early and the others are unable to sustain their challenge, allowing a controlled, measured gallop.
scenarios.body: A lone leader settles into a rhythm and conserves enough energy to maintain momentum through the Salisbury straight, rewarding front-running grit rather than a late surge; Takeitorleaveit's consistent placed record from the front suits this shape particularly well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace combusts completely and the field strings out, leaving ground for closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Mid Flight or Scarlet Letter, racing entirely unpressured at the rear, benefit from a truly-run race collapsing the front rank and find clear running in the straight; soft-ground stamina and a patient ride are the keys in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Midfield Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace produces a messy race with interference, checks, and a compressed mid-race tempo that suits a prominent-to-midfield finisher.
scenarios.body: Sax Avoidance or Miss Guinevere, travelling smoothly in the slipstream without fighting for position, find themselves ideally placed when the pace falters mid-race and benefit from clear running; neither is a natural leader, and the lack of early pressure allows them to travel without undue cost.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Relentless Hero and Next Guilian can actually secure front-running berths without fighting each other wide — if both have to work hard for position, they risk compromising their own stamina before the race truly begins.

Eljowhary's fade-in-finish flag combined with prominent running style means Charles Bishop may be forced to make a decision at halfway; if he drops in to conserve, he adds to midfield congestion, and if he persists up front he is a spent force at the business end.

Gatlinburg's 105-day absence for a yard (Attwater, 1/12 in 14 days) that is not firing at present means fitness is genuinely uncertain — if she comes with a late run she could surprise, but the layoff in soft ground on a stiff track is a risk combination.

The going report confirms good-to-soft across every race on the card — no degradation to soft yet — which may marginally assist the front-runners' stamina relative to a full soft scenario, keeping Takeitorleaveit's claims alive longer than expected.

Draw has minimal impact in a 10-runner 1m2f at Salisbury on this going, but watch whether the three inside draws (Mid Flight 1, Gatlinburg 2, Takeitorleaveit 3) allow quiet passage to position without early traffic issues in the early part of the race.
